approved: Joe, 2026-11-14 ("yes to all", via the channel-learner session)
notes: The ids are the contract. Names, definitions and examples may be reworded without a version change. Adding a job is a minor version (1.1); renaming, splitting, merging or removing one is a major version (2) and ships with a mapping. Joe approves every change; the channel learner and briefs only propose. Recipes that serve no job are tagged build-aid; recipes that fit no job are tagged unmatched and proposed.

groups.line: Line jobs: what the viewer must get from this line
groups.picture: Picture jobs: how the picture has to read, whatever the line says
groups.connective: Connective jobs: between and across pictures

tags.build-aid: A recipe that helps build but serves no beat (shy layers, Grow Bounds, shutter angle, crisp precomps). Never returned by a beat query.
tags.unmatched: A recipe that fits no job yet. Goes to the proposals queue; never becomes a job without Joe.

jobs.name: Land a number
jobs.definition: Make one figure arrive, hit and stay readable, so the viewer remembers it.
jobs.example: "$212 a month" on the spending reel

jobs.name: Make a quantity countable
jobs.definition: Show how many as objects the eye can count, not as a numeral.
jobs.example: "20 agents" as 20 discs that settle on the count

jobs.name: Make time felt
jobs.definition: Show a duration, speed or deadline as something that fills, runs or stops.
jobs.example: "under two seconds" as a timer that stops on the word

jobs.name: Build a list
jobs.definition: Bring in n things one at a time, each staying as the next arrives.
jobs.example: the three tools Joe uses, one per word

jobs.name: Show a process step by step
jobs.definition: Show a sequence where each step lights as it is named and the order reads.
jobs.example: script, brief, build, render along one rail

jobs.name: Set two things side by side
jobs.definition: Put this against that (old way and new, theirs and mine) so the difference reads at a glance.
jobs.example: doing it by hand against the agent doing it

jobs.name: Show a change of state
jobs.definition: Show the same thing before and after one change, with the change itself visible.
jobs.example: the raw clip, then the graded clip

jobs.name: Fail, then fix
jobs.definition: Show something going wrong, then the fix making it right, as a story beat.
jobs.example: the first build breaks red, the second runs green

jobs.name: One becomes many, or many become one
jobs.definition: Show a fan-out or a gathering: copies, sources, a hub and its spokes.
jobs.example: one prompt sent to five agents

jobs.name: Tie things together or keep them apart
jobs.definition: Draw a relation (connected, flows into, walled off) on its connective word.
jobs.example: "connected" as an arc drawn between two apps

jobs.name: Make an abstract idea concrete
jobs.definition: Give an abstract line one object or small scene that acts it out.
jobs.example: "memory" as a notebook the agent writes in

jobs.name: Show a real screen
jobs.definition: Present a real app, page or recording so it reads at phone size and the viewer knows where to look.
jobs.example: Joe clicking through Claude's settings

jobs.name: Introduce a named tool
jobs.definition: Put a named product on screen with its real mark, so the viewer can find it later.
jobs.example: "Higgsfield" with its logo

jobs.name: Show proof
jobs.definition: Present a real result (a chart, a score, a receipt) as evidence for the claim.
jobs.example: the reel's real views chart

jobs.name: Reveal a headline
jobs.definition: Land a title, statement or quote in type, word by word or as one block.
jobs.example: a section title; a full-screen claim

jobs.name: Point at the detail
jobs.definition: Send the eye to one part of a held picture: a box, a ring, a push, a note.
jobs.example: circling the one line in the terms that matters

jobs.name: Flag a problem
jobs.definition: Mark a risk, a warning or a wrong answer so it reads as wrong before it is explained.
jobs.example: "don't paste your API key here"

jobs.name: Ask for the action
jobs.definition: Make the ask and its keyword unmissable at the end.
jobs.example: "Comment GUIDE" on the offer card

jobs.name: Establish a place
jobs.definition: Set a world or location in one frame so the viewer knows where they are.
jobs.example: the night scene: the bed, the moon, the agent at work

jobs.name: Add depth to a flat scene
jobs.definition: Make flat layers read as one space: shadow, fog, focus, parallax, a 3D floor.
jobs.example: the cast sitting on the mat with a real shadow

jobs.name: Light the hero
jobs.definition: Make one object the lit thing in the frame and let the rest fall back.
jobs.example: the capsule on "Spin it off"

jobs.name: Give a held picture a living backdrop
jobs.definition: A background that moves or textures quietly under a held picture without competing.
jobs.example: a dot grid or drifting light under a GRAPHIC list

jobs.name: Finish and unify the look
jobs.definition: A pass over a section or the whole reel (grade, grain, bloom, texture) that makes mixed parts read as one piece.
jobs.example: stock logos and Blender renders pulled into one palette

jobs.name: Add impact on a word
jobs.definition: A short accent (burst, shake, particles, flash) on a stressed word or a peak.
jobs.example: the beat the reel's number lands

jobs.name: Hand over to the next picture
jobs.definition: Change picture without it reading as a cut: travel, grow, exchange, whip, carry, line-led. Covers a transition on a beat.
jobs.example: the camera travels right along the film strip into the pipeline

jobs.name: Move the camera with a motive
jobs.definition: A move inside a picture that something leads (a line, an arrival, the part being said).
jobs.example: push in on the step that lights

jobs.name: Keep a held picture alive
jobs.definition: Slow drift, loop or orbit so a held frame never goes still.
jobs.example: a ring of cards turning slowly under the face card
